But if you have a material ID with leading zeroes followed by alphanumeric values (for exampe, 000X12), then the zeros will remain.-Resolution-This is the expected system behavior.-Keywords-Material ID, Leading Zero, Alpha-Conversion, Alphanumeric

Title: Error While Creating Business Partner: "Number Range Depleted"
Content: Symptom-You are trying to create a new business partner (for example, a service agent), but the creation fails with error message "Number range depleted".-Environment-SAP Cloud for Customers-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Business Partner work center-Access the Service Agent work center view.-Click the New button, then select Service Agent.-Maintain all mandatory fields.-Click Save or Save and Close.-Error message "Number range depleted" is raised.-Cause-The error is raised when you try to exceed the limit of the number range maintained for Business partners. Most business partners (like accounts, contacts, etc.) share the same number range and the error can be raised while creating any of them.-Resolution-Please extend the number ranges for business partners by following the steps below.-Go to Business Configuration work center.-Access the Overview work center view.-Search and open the activity General Business Partners.-Select Define Number Ranges for Business Partners.-Maintain the number ranges as required.-Note:-It is not possible to create different number range specific for accounts, contacts, business partners.-When you create a business partner, you may use internal number ranges if you want the system to automatically assign a number.-When you create a business partner, you may use external number ranges if you want to enter the number manually.-Create number ranges with sufficient intervals to avoid future complications.-Ensure that the intervals of internal and external number ranges do not overlap.-Ensure that the ID length specified is not shorter than the length of any IDs that are currently in use in the system.-Changing previously assigned number ranges can lead to problems in the system.-If a business partner is already available in the system, you would not be able to change the beginning number of the number range interval, as there is a veto check in the backend that blocks the change if the ID of an existing business partner would be left outside the new number range. As such, the goal is always to change the end number of the interval to allow for new values (always observing that existing number ranges do not overlap).-It is not possible to delete the master data (accounts, contacts, business partners etc.) once it is created in the system.-The internal number ranges are used automatically by the solution during productive use, for example, if you create the data directly in the work centers' UI.-We recommend that you use the predefined number ranges.-Change the predefined number ranges only if necessary and mind the consequences.-When you create business partners using the web services, where you manually specify the IDs in the request payload, the numbers will be taken from the external number range. When you create them using web services, where you do not specify the IDs in the request payload, the numbers will be automatically taken from the internal number range. The same applies for Data Workbench/OData as well.-The external number range from "A" to "ZZZZZZZZZZ" is not open for editing and cannot be changed. The allowed characters are: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-/:\." -This interval allows to maintain alphanumerical IDs for business partners, but IDs must always start with a letter. So, for example ".A123" is not allowed but "A.123" is allowed.-See Also-Determine your Strategy for Number Range Assignment-Account ID range in C4C-Keywords-Business Partners, business partner number range assignment, individual customers, accounts, account, contacts, contact, supplier

Title: No Automatic Clearing of Open Items when Checking Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations
Content: Symptom-Automatic Bank Statements containing transactions for open invoices (payables/receivables) are uploaded and posted.-There are no Rules for Analyzing Memo Lines defined and there are not external document numbers referenced in the memo-line of respective bank statement blocks.-Notwithstanding this, an automatic clearing of open invoices is expected based on:-Pertinent settings for Clearing Strategies which allow for Clearings without External Reference.-Previous Payment Clearings and the selection of 'Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations' checkbox in associated Payment Allocations of that type.-After posting of a Bank Statement, however, On Account Payments are created automatically. Suitable invoices did not get cleared.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue-To check the Clearing Strategies:-In the Business Configuration workcenter navigate to the Overview.-Find the Clearing Strategies activity. Or, if your system is not live yet, access this activity from Fine Tuning in the Implementation Project.-Choose Maintain clearing strategies.-Besides settings for Tolerances you can define Allow Automatic Clearing If No or Incorrect Reference Number under Further Settings.-To check the indicator 'Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations' in Payment Allocations:-After a previous Bank Statement posting the Postprocessing status would have shown as Required, in this case, indicating a Payment Allocation in 'In Preparation' status. The Payment Allocation can be accessed either in the Liquidity Management workcenter, via the bank statement itself or in the Payment Management workcenter.-Liquidity Management workcenter:-In the Bank Statement view Select the relevant posted bank statement.-In the Postprocessing column, follow the Required link.-Payment Management workcenter:-Navigate to the Payment Allocation view.-Select the relevant payment allocation of type 'Bank Statement', Status 'In Preparation'.-In the first Payment Allocation ABC resulting from a previous bank statement posting:-Navigate to the  Customer/Supplier tab and specify the intended business partner account XYZ. The Open Items grid will fill with open receivables/payables items.-Match corresponding transactions with suitable due-items until the Open Amount of the Payment Allocation is 0,00.-Mark the tick-box Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations and press Post.-Payment Allocation DEF resulting from a subsequent bank statement posting:-Payment Allocation DEF and associated Payment Clearing are automatically posted (Postprocessing status: Not Required); However, the allocation was posted  as an On Account Payment for Customer/Supplier XYZ. Open invoices are not cleared.-Cause-It is a system definition that automatic Payment Allocations solely based on the indicator Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations result in On Account Payments against Customer/Supplier (The identification usually is based on the IBAN-Number in the Bank Statement memo).-Settings for Clearings without External Reference in Payment Strategies do not apply for such a Payment Allocation from Bank Statement.-Resolution-In such a scenario open due-times will have to be cleared in the Account Monitor, e.g. Customer Account Monitor.-Navigate to Receivables work center.-Customers / Customer Accounts view.-Select customer account XYZ and open the Customer Account Monitor via View.-On Account Payment from Payment Allocation DEF here shows with External Reference of the Bank Statement Item and has to be matched with a suitable open Invoice.-An automatic invoice clearing in Payment Allocation DEF already when posting the Bank Statement can be achieved by additionally setting up Rules for Analyzing Memo Lines in case open receivables/payables are referenced in the Bank Statement itself.-For creation and testing of such rules please consult the Online-Help: Creation of Memo Line Analysis Rules for Common Use Cases.-Keywords-No Automatic Clearing of Open Items when Checking Remember Assignment for Future Payment Allocations; IBAN-Number; Automatic Bank Statements; Payment Allocations; Automatic Clearing.

Title: Error in Payment Allocation: Company Does not Exist or is Invalid or not Accessible
Content: Symptom-You are posting a payment allocation, however an error message informing that the company is not accessible or invalid is being raised.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Payment Management work center. -Go to Payment Allocation view.-Find and open the respective payment allocation.-Click Post.-The following error is being raised:  'Company <Company ID and name> does not exist or is invalid or not accessible'-Cause-The error is raised because there is a bank statement item with Value Date outside the company's validity period.-In the Payment Allocation, you can click View All and refer to the Original Payment section to check the corresponding dates. By opening the related bank statement, the same can be seen via the bank statement item.-Resolution-You need to either re-create the bank statement with the Value Dates within the company's validity period or adjust the Valid From date of the Org. Unit backwards to cover the Value Date from the bank statement item. The org. unit validity can be adjusted via Organizational Management work center.-Keywords-Bank Statement, Payment Allocation, Org. Unit, Company does not exist

Title: New Fixed Asset Creation Error 'Valid Fixed Asset Class Missing, Enter Valid Fixed Asset Class'
Content: Symptom-When creating a new fixed asset you notice the following:-In the Fixed Asset Class field's valuation help no fixed asset classes are displayed. Instead, the message 'No items found' appears.-The error message 'Valid fixed asset class missing, enter valid fixed asset class' appears.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Fixed Assets work center.-Choose New Fixed Asset under Common Tasks.-In the New Fixed Asset screen, enter the Fixed Asset Description.-Specify the Company XYZ (XYZ represents the Company ID).-The Fixed Asset Class field's dropdown menu shows the message 'No items found'.-The error message 'Valid fixed asset class missing, enter valid fixed asset class' is displayed.-Cause-The Fixed Asset Class on the Fixed Asset creation screen is based on the Valuation Views assigned in the 'Fixed Asset Classes' fine-tune activity. All the Valuation Views assigned to all the Set of Books of the Company XYZ need to be assigned in this activity and be active.-Resolution-To fix the issue and successfully create the fixed asset, please follow the steps below:-A) Steps to check the Valuation Views assigned to the Set of Books for Company XYZ.-Note: If the Company XYZ uses more than one Set of Books you need to assign all Valuation Views of all Set of Books.-Go to the Business Configuration workcenter.-Go to the Implementation projects view.-Open the Activity List.-Open the Integrate and Extend phase.-Open the activity called 'Set of Books'.-Select the Set of Books that is assigned to the Company XYZ.-Click Edit.-Open the Fixed Asset Settings tab.-Note: You can see Valuation Views and check if they are on Active status.-B) Steps to maintain the relevant Valuation Views for the Fixed Asset Class that you want to use when creating the new fixed asset:-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Go to the Implementation Projects.-Open the Activity List.-Open the Fine-Tune phase.-Open the 'Fixed Asset Classes' activity.-Click the 'Edit fixed asset classes' hyperlink.-Select the relevant Fixed Asset Class.-Open the Default Valuation Settings tab.-Click the Add row button.-Enter the relevant Valuation Views, the Valuation Views that are assigned to the Set of Books for Company XYZ.-Maintain all other relevant data.-Click the Save and Close button.-You are now able to select the Fixed Asset Class dropdown list when creating new fixed assets.-Keywords-Fixed Asset, Class, New, Creation, Error, Valid, Maintain, Missing, Valuation View, Business Configuration, Company

Title: "The Request Was Aborted: Could Not Create SSL/TLS Secure Channel" While Trying to Log On To an Add-In
Content: Symptom-You're trying to log on to the Outlook or Excel add-ins for SAP Cloud for Customer or SAP Business ByDesign, but error message "The request was aborted: could not create SSL/TLS secure channel" is raised.-Image/data in this KBA is from SAP internal systems, sample data, or demo systems. Any resemblance to real data is purely coincidental.-Environment-SAP Cloud For Customer-SAP Business ByDesign-Cause-You're using TLSv1.0 protocol, which is no longer supported.-As a part of our commitment to continuous improvement and to follow industries best practices, we plan to configure our servers to support only the latest protocol versions TLSv1.1 and TLSv1.2.-Resolution-To solve this error, you must ensure .NET Framework is using SSL/TLS 1.1 on Windows settings.-There are two options for solving this: editing the Windows registry or reinstalling the .NET Framework.-1) Editing the Windows registry:-Please ensure that you have the below settings enabled in your Windows machine to avoid connectivity issues from SAP Cloud For Customer and SAP Business ByDesign application add-ons:-In your Windows PC, go to Windows search and type "Regedit".-Click the Yes button; it opens the Registry Editor.-Open the path below based on the version of .NET Framework installed on your machine, in this case it is 4.0.30319:-Please note: It needs to be done on both paths below. -Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework\v4.0.30319-Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\.NETFramework\v 4.0.30319-If you find the value defined as 0 instead of 1, follow below steps to change “data” from 0 to 1 and further test the result:-Key: Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework\v4.0.30319 -Value: SchUseStrongCrypto-Type: REG_DWORD-Data: 1-Key:Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\.NETFramework\v4.0.30319-Value: SchUseStrongCrypto-Type: REG_DWORD-Data: 1-If you don't find the "SchUseStrongCrypto" in your registry inside one or both of the .NET Framework paths, please create one by following the steps below:-Please note: Your machine account will need to have administrator privileges.-Right-click in the empty space.-Select New.-Click the DWORD (32-bit) Value.-Type the name "SchUseStrongCrypto" for the newly created entry.-Double-click "SchUseStrongCrypto" again to edit it.-Make sure that Value Data is 1. -2) Reinstalling the .NET Framework:-If you still find an issue with SAP Cloud For Customer/SAP Business ByDesign add-ins connecting to the application or if the registry is already set to 1, then reinstall the .NET Framework to 4.6.2 or higher versions and perform the above steps again for this newer version.-How to reinstall .NET Framework:-In your Windows PC, go to Windows search and type "Turn Windows features on or off."-Deselect the checkboxes related to .NET Framework.-Click the Ok button.-Windows will uninstall .NET Framework. When it is finished, go back to "Turn Windows features on or off."-Select the checkboxes related to .NET Framework again.-Select "Let Windows Update download the files for you." This will install and update it.-  See Also-SAP Community blog "Disabling TLSv1.0 protocol and 3DES cipher suite for Inbound communication to ByD"-Keywords-TLS; Logon; SSL; Outlook; Excel: Add-in; Add-on;  el; TLS v1.0; TLS v1.1; .NET Framework

Title: '500 SAP Internal Server Error ERROR: Semantic Descriptor Does not Exist (Termination: ERROR_MESSAGE_STATE)' During Migration of Open Items Receivables
Content: Message Strip Error-Warning: This Note/KBA is not yet released to customers. Please do not share it with them.-Symptom-***INTERNAL USE ONLY***-When migrating accounting data (e.g. Open Items Receivables) using the migration tool in Business Configuration, the following error occurs.-File validation failed. Create an incident.-When you attempt to download the file, the following error occurs in your browser:-"500 SAP Internal Server Error-ERROR: Semantic descriptor does not exist (termination: ERROR_MESSAGE_STATE)."-OR-While downloading the migration template for Open Items Receivables you get the error message:-"500 SAP Internal Server Error-ERROR: Semantic descriptor does not exist (termination: ERROR_MESSAGE_STATE)."-"Image/data in this KBA is from SAP internal systems, sample data, or demo systems. Any resemblance to real data is purely coincidental."-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Go to the Overview subview.-Search and open Activity: Migration of Accounting Transaction.-Click the Migrate accounting transaction data using the migration tool link.-Select effected migration unit -> this is in status In Process and has the Title ABC (ABC is the title of the migration unit) for company XYZ (XYZ is the company ID).-Click the Execute Migration button.-Select the Open Items Receivable file and click the Process File button.-The error message is  File validation failed. Create an incident.-Click the Repeat Validation -> Validate all records button.-The error message is File validation failed. Create an incident.-Click the Exit Process file button.-Select the Open Items Receivable file again.-Click the Action button and select Download.-The error message is:-"500 SAP Internal Server Error-Semantic descriptor does not exist (termination: ERROR_MESSAGE_STATE)".-  In the Overview subview of the Business Configuration work center.-Search and open activity Perform Data Extraction.-Click Download Migration Templates.-Under Transaction Data Financial Accounting select Open Items Receivables.-Click Download.-The error message is:-"500 SAP Internal Server Error-Semantic descriptor does not exist (termination: ERROR_MESSAGE_STATE)."-Resolution-Please make sure that the Migration tool is completely closed in the frontend before proceeding to the below mentioned steps:-Log in to the Backend-Enter the transaction DMC_INC_CORR. This is the DMC_INCONSISTENCY_CORR_REPORT for checking the object consistency (Inconsistency Issues Correction Report).-Choose the migration object for which this report should be executed.-In this case it is OPEN_ITMS_RECEI001 and can be selected at the Migration Object.-  Check the “Check Object Consistency” checkbox.-Click Execute.-The error message is as below:-  Go back to the previous screen.-Check the Generate Run Time Object checkbox.-Click execute.-You get the error message:-    Go back to the previous screen (you might be thrown out of the DMC_INC_CORR transaction). If yes, enter the transaction DMC_INC_CORR again.-In the new screen, check the No Semantic Descriptor Exist checkbox and click execute.-  If the issue is corrected, you get the screen below:-  If the system dumps please forward to development for correction.-Now login in to the frontend again and check if the issue is corrected.-In the Overview subview of the Business Configuration work center.-Search and open activity Perform Data Extraction.-Click Download Migration Templates.-Under Transaction Data Financial Accounting select Open Items Receivables.-Click Download.-Download is successful. The semantic error is resolved.-Now try to reproduce the error for the migration file customer has created.-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Go to the Overview subview.-Search and open Activity: Migration of Accounting Transaction.-Click the Migrate accounting transaction data using the migration tool link.-Select effected migration unit -> this is in status In Process and has the Title ABC for company XYZ.-Click the Execute Migration button.-Select the Open Items Receivable file and click the Process File button.- You can revert to customer with appropriate message.-Keywords-Semantic Descriptor Does not Exist; Migration; Open Items Receivables; Forderungen; Migrationsvorlage

Title: The Sender ID, Receiver ID, Sender Type and Receiver Type columns are missing from Excel File of an Overhead Distribution
Content: Symptom-You are exporting the successfully processed log of an Overhead Distribution run to Microsoft Excel. -In the exported Excel list you notice that the Sender ID, Receiver ID, Sender Type and Receiver Type are not displayed in the list. -Environment- SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Cost and Revenue work center.-Go to the Overhead Distribution view.-Search and Select the respective Run ID.-Under Details, in the Logs collumn press Log Results.-In the application log go to the Processed Successfully tab.-Press Export - To Microsoft Excel.-Open the file.-You notice that the Sender ID, Receiver ID, Sender Type and Receiver Type are not displayed in the list.-Cause-The Sender ID, Receiver ID, Sender Type and Receiver Type fields are so called calculated fields-Resolution-The export to Microsoft Excel is not supported for calculated fields. The system behaves as expected.-Keywords-Sender ID, Receiver ID, Sender Type, Receiver Type, columns missing, Excel File, Overhead Distribution.

Title: Action not Enabled Error When Creating Outbound File for Payments
Content: Symptom-You are selecting a batch of bank transfers from the Payment Monitor to create the corresponding payment file, however both success and failure messages appear.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Payment Management work center.-Go to Payment Monitor view.-Show bank transfers that are Ready for Transfer.-Select multiple bank transfers at the same time.-Click Actions for bank Transactions and click to create the payment file.-The following messages are raised:-Payment file created successfully-Action not enabled-Cause-Within the selected bank transfers batch, there is at least one bank transfer whose payment media format is 'Manual Payment'. Hence, when you trigger the create payment file action for all selected payments, the system would also try to create an outbound file for the manual payment. However, since the media format is manual payment, this entails a manual action by the user in the bank's system to perform the payment. Hence, no outbound file is required and the action is therefore disabled for such payments.-Resolution-In such cases, you need to revise the selected payments and pay the bank transfers with Manual Payment format separately. You are then able to trigger the outbound file creation for a batch of payments that have no Manual Payments in it.-Keywords-Liquidity Management. Payment monitor. Payment Management. Outgoing Bank Transfer. Payment Format. Outbound File.

Title: No Electronic Payment Documents Were Generated in Electronic Payment Run for Mexico
Content: Symptom-This KBA is specific for Mexico localization.-You have made an Electronic Payment run, and after running a job the Application Log shows the message "No se generaron documentos de pago electrónico", or "No Electronic Payment Documents were generated".-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Receivables work center.-Go to the Electronic Payment Run view.-Search for the run AAA. (AAA = Run ID)-Open the Application Log BBB. (BBB = Application Log ID)-In the General tab, you will see the message "No se generaron documentos de pago electrónico", or in English "No Electronic Payment Documents were generated".-Cause-The run settings link it to a specific payment or customer account. The payment you expect to see in the run is linked to a Customer Invoice XXX (XXX = Customer Invoice ID), which itself is linked to two clearings: ABC and XYZ. (ABC and XYZ = Clearing IDs)-Clearing XYZ is canceled, and clearing ABC is the new clearing created after XYZ's cancellation.-The Clearing ID XYZ is included in one or more Electronic Payment Documents, which you can find by going to the Receivables work center, Electronic Payment Documents view. Due to these Electronic Payment Documents already generated, the system does not create new Electronic Payments in the run.-Resolution-An Electronic Payment Document for a respective Payment or Clearing must be canceled explicitly in case the original Payment/Clearing is canceled. This shall capture latest payment or clearing details on new electronic payment document.-You can cancel the Electronic Payment Documents involving the canceled Clearing, and regenerate electronic payment documents for the respective posting date period.-Keywords-Electronic Payment, Mexico, run, no payment generated

Title: Not Able to Post a Journal Entry Voucher Due to Error: ‘500 SAP Internal Server Error’
Content: Symptom-You are trying to post a Journal Entry Voucher document but is receiving the error message ‘500 SAP Internal Server Error’.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to General Ledger work center.-Go to Journal Entry Vouchers subview.-Select the option Not Posted Journal Entry Vouchers.-Search for Journal Entry Voucher ID XYZ (XYZ represents the Journal Entry Voucher ID).-Click Edit.-Click Post .-You will see the error message: -Please try resuming your work. If you still face issues, report an incident.-Details-ClassName-sap.b.controller.event.PostRequest-MethodName-post-Response-500 SAP Internal Server Error-500 SAP Internal Server Error-Cause-One possible reason for such issue is that when the G/L account or account assignment on one of the lines has been changed, the roundtrip doesn't trigger, so there is an unexpected sub-ledger account line-item type.-Resolution-Remove the line and add it again.-If the G/L Account is required to be changed on a line, the recommendation is to add a new line fresh for this G/L Account instead of modifying what's there already.-Keywords-Journal Entry Voucher. 500 SAP Internal Server Error. Post Journal Entry document. Dump

Title: Profit Center is Missing in a Journal Entry Created From a Journal Entry Voucher
Content: Symptom-The Profit Center ID field is blank for a line item in a Journal Entry created from a Journal Entry Voucher.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the General Ledger work center.-Go to the Journal Entries view.-Open Journal Entry ID AAA (AAA means the Journal Entry ID).-Select Line Item ID BBB (BBB means the Line Item ID).-Notice that Profit Center ID field is blank, while for Line Item ID CCC there's a Profit Center ID retrieved.-CCC means the Line Item ID.-Cause-In the preceding document, which is Journal Entry Voucher DDD (DDD means the Journal Entry Voucher ID) for the respective line item the Changed Profit Center/Segment checkbox has been marked and then the Profit Center ID field has been left blank. When this checkbox is flagged, the automatic derivation of profit center in the resulting journal entry is overridden, and since the Profit Center was left blank, this information (no Profit Center) is retrieved in the resulting journal entry.-Resolution-System behaves as designed.-See Also-Journal Entry Vouchers Quick Guide-Keywords-journal entry voucher; JEV; changed profit center; JE; journal entry

Title: Purchase Request Bundling Run is Creating Purchase Orders with Warning Message
Content: Symptom-Purchase Request Bundling Run creates Purchase Orders even though there is a warning message.-Environment- SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Purchase Requests and Orders work center.-Go to Purchase Request Bundling Runs view.-Select the run.-Show: All Logs.-Select the Application Log.-Open it.-Navigate to Results tab.-You can see the description:-The purchase order value is lower than the minimum purchase order value defined in the supplier master.-Purchase order ABC created-You didn't expect that the system would create a Purchase Order which has a warning message.-Cause-The 'Minimum Purchase Order Value' won't block the Purchase Order from being created.-It's the same scenario as when you try to create a Purchase Order with a product which has price as zero. The system triggers a warning message regarding that the value is too low, however, you'll be able to post it anyway.-Resolution-System standard behavior.-Keywords-Purchase Order, Purchase Request Bundling Run, Minimum Purchase Order Value, Run

Title: Payer/Payee Details not Displayed in Journal Entry Resulting from Payment Allocation
Content: Symptom-You have allocated Payment to G/L Account in Payment Allocation and have maintained Payer/Payee field. However, you are unable to see Payer/Payee details in the Payment Allocation Journal Entry.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Payment Management work center.-Go to the Payment Allocation view.-Show All Payment Allocations and find the respective Payment Allocation.-Go to Allocation to G/L Account tab.-You could see that the G/L Account and Payer/Payee details are maintained and choose post.-The Journal Entry which gets created does not show Payer/Payee details (for example, Partner Company ID and Partner Company Name).-Cause-The Payer/Payee entered in the payment allocation is a partner company, hence you expect the system to derive the data in the journal entry. However the G/L Account entered is a balance sheet account (for example, of G/L Account Type OASSET - Other assets). For balance sheet accounts they system only derive the partner company if the G/L Account is open item managed.-Resolution-The system behaves as expected here.-To have the Partner Company entered in Payer/Payee field in the payment allocation derived in the journal entry, the G/L Account entered along with it should not be a balance sheet account, OR, in case of a balance sheet account, it must be open item managed (Open Item Management checkbox flagged in Chart of Accounts).-See Also-Help Document: Account Type-Keywords-payer/payee; partner company id; partner company name; balance sheet account; open item management

Title: How to Locate Specific Products Assigned to Product Categories
Content: Message Strip Error-Warning: This Note/KBA is not yet released to customers. Please do not share it with them.-Symptom-You are trying to remove the Product Assignment Indicator from a product category, but system throws error message: "Cannot undo Product Assignment for XYZ; there are products assigned to it" (where XYZ is stands for an actual product category ID).-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Product and Service Portfolio work center-Access the Product Categories work center view-Click Maintain Product Categories-Select the appropriate Product Category-Uncheck the Product Assignment box-Note: Now, how user can locate specific products assigned to product categories? so those products can be unassigned to resolve the issue.-Resolution-Login to backend and enter t-code SESFTS-In the test shell, open BO: PDM_PRODUCT-Query by Identification - by ID, provide the Product Category Internal IDs-This will list the products with the product category assignment-Share the products details that are assigned to the Product Categories to customer and they can Unassign the Product Categories from those Products-See Also-You can also refer to the KBA - 2480314-Keywords-Unassign product, Locate products

Title: Assign Multiple Tax Payments to One Tax Return
Content: Symptom-You want to assign multiple tax payments to one tax return.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Tax Management work center.-Go to the Periodic Tasks view.-Go to the Sales and Use Tax Returns Runs view.-Perform the action New Tax Return Run to create a new tax return.-This will create a new Tax Return ABC (ABC means the Tax Return ID).-Go to the Payment Management work center.-Go to the Common Tasks view and perform the action New Outgoing Check/New Outgoing Bank Transfer.-Input the Payee field as Tax Authority XYZ (XYZ means the Tax Authority ID).-Post this payment and this will create a new Tax Payment.-Go to the Tax Management work center.-Go to the Tax Payments view.-Here you will see the newly created Tax Payment for the Tax Authority XYZ.-You are now creating multiple tax payments and then want to assign these to one Tax Return ABC.-Resolution-The system is not supporting partial tax payment clearing. This means you won't be able to assign multiple tax payments to one sales and use tax return.-To correct the existing data, you have to reverse the outgoing checks and create a single check and assign the tax return to the tax payment created, as follows:-Go to the Payment Management work center.-Go to the Payment Monitor view.-Select the outgoing checks and perform the action Set to Not Transferred.-The status of the check will move to Ready to Transfer.-Perform the action Reverse which will cancel this check and the Tax Payment created will be moved to Release discarded.-You have to do this for all the outgoing checks/bank transfers which you already created. You can later create a single outgoing check / bank transfer with the same amount.-If there is a difference then you have to accept that and later post the tax payment by assigning the tax returns. The tax returns status will change from Reported to Completed.-See Also-Help Document: Tax Payments Quick Guide-Keywords-multiple tax payments; tax return; sales and use; vat return

Title: How to update the C4C Domain Certificate?
Content: Symptom-How to update the C4C Domain Certificate (*.c4c.cloud.sap)?-Environment-SAP Cloud for Customer-Reproducing the Issue-As part of infrastructure migration, and standard practice for SSL certificates it is recommended to use SAN extension for which your existing *.crm.ondemand.com domain certificate is incorporated with Multi Domain SSL Certificate feature.-Cause-If you have third-party integrations like web services/APIs in your Cloud for Customer tenants, you may be required to update the domain certificate. These updates should be conducted by your internal IT resources, with the new certificate information that could be found below-Resolution-Below are the steps to download the new certificate:-1. Click on download link. You will be redirected to Digi Cert Website, here ensure Combined Certificate Files are set as shown below.-2. Click download as shown below.-3. A zip file by name: star_c4c_cloud_sap_216916196 would be downloaded.-4. Please unzip this file and we can see the required certificate star_c4c_cloud_sap.crt which you need to adapt for running integration scenarios.-  See Also-3199761 - FAQs -How to update C4C Domain Certificate

Title: Purchase Order Item is not Showing in Report Purchase Order History
Content: Symptom-Purchase Order's item is not showing in report Purchase Order History-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Purchase Requests and Orders work center.-Go to Reports view.-Open report Purchase Order History. -In Selection section, insert the Purchase Order's ID. -Click in Apply.-You can see that it's missing a Purchase Order's item here.-Cause-The report Purchase Order History only shows items that have a follow-up document or if the item has the configuration: Delivery Status is 'Not Delivered' and Invoice Status is 'Not Invoiced' or 'Not Relevant'.-Also if an item is linked to a Supplier Invoice (even though it's voided), this item is shown in the report.-Resolution-This is the system's standard behavior.-Keywords-Purchase Order History, Report, Delivery Status, Invoice Status, Item, Purchase Order

Title: 'No active account found for VRN GBXXX' Error Upon Submission of UK MTD VAT Return
Content: Symptom-Error message after submission of UK VAT Return:-'No active account found for VRN GBXXX.|Technical Response: Missing required parameter: Client / Account Registration Located in: REMOTE_CONNECTOR-PROCESS_DATA'-GBXXX means the VAT Registration Number for UK Making Tax Digital (MTD).-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Tax Management work center.-Go to the VAT Returns view.-Find and open respective Tax Return ID.-Click View All.-Under Submission Information section, notice the Error Description:-'No active account found for VRN GBXXX.|Technical Response: Missing required parameter: Client / Account Registration Located in: REMOTE_CONNECTOR-PROCESS_DATA'-Cause-The granted access for GBXXX has expired. Ideally the granted access is valid for 18 months.-Resolution-You have to reauthorize SAP Business ByDesign system for MTD submission using the activity UK Making Tax Digital in Business Configuration work center.-Post the activity has been re-performed the submission should go through.-Keywords-UK MTD; VAT Registration Number; making tax digital; active account

Title: How to Extract Holiday Calendar Codes in SAP Business ByDesign
Content: Symptom-You want to extract holiday calendar codes, to find out if they match with the ones in Success Factors. But you don't find any option to see all existing holiday calendar codes.-Environment- SAP Business ByDesign-Cause-There is currently no report that will show the list of available codes for the holiday calendars in a system.-Resolution-You may use the following workaround:-Go to Time Administration-Select Regular Task view-Select Maintain Deviating Holiday Calendar option-Enter any employee ID-Add a row (without saving)-Use the value help on the field Public Holiday Calendar-Find a list of the available holiday calendars-Keywords-missing not available unavailable search export see

Title: Why The Point of Sales Document Are Being Interrupted
Content: Symptom-There are some SAP customer checkout tickets that failed showing as interrupted.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Application and User Management work center.-Select the view Business Communication Monitoring.-Search for the Business Document: Point-of-Sale Transaction.-The query will retrieve the Point-of-Sale Transaction ID ABC (Where ABC represents your Point-of-Sale Transaction ID) which are failed.-Cause-It is happening because a duplicate request has been sent from the external system to Business ByDesign.-Resolution-This is the expected system behavior.-Keywords-Point of Sales; Business Communication Monitoring; customer checkout

Title: POB Allocated Invoiced Amount Different to Sales Order Item's Invoiced Revenue Amount
Content: Symptom-You complete all items of a Sales Order. When checking the POB IDs of the associated  Revenue Acccounting Contract (RAC) you notice that the Allocated Invoiced Amounts of the POB items are different to the associated Sales Order items' Invoiced Revenue amounts.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-In the Cost and Revenue work center go to the Sales Document items view. -Use the Sales Order Items view. -Select the items of Sales Order ABC by searching for ABC* in the search field (ABC represents the Sales Order ID).-The items ABC-AA, BB, CC, DD appear. (AA, BB, CC, DD represent different Sales Order item IDs). -First, navigate to the Dates tab and verify that for all items a Final Delivery or Invoice Date is displayed. -Then, access the RAC XYZ from the Revenue Accounting Contract collumn (XYZ represents the RAC ID). -After a Sales Document Item is completed the Allocated Invoice amount is automatically calculated for the associated POB ID (You might have to add the Allocated Invoiced Amount collumn to the screen via Personalization Mode). -You notice that the Allocated Invoiced Amount of the POB IDs is different to the Invoiced Revenue amounts of the Sales Order items.-You also notice that the total  Invoiced Revenue amount equals the total Allocated Invoiced Amount. Example is as follows.-In the Sales Document Items view select item ABC-AA.-Navigate to the Accounting Data tab. -Here, the Invoiced Revenue appears: -750,00 LC (LC=Local Currency). -Access the RAC. -The associated POB ID XYZ-AA displays an Allocated Invoiced Amount of 640,00 LC. -Check the other Sales Order Items and associated POBs. You notice the sales order items' Invoiced Revenue amounts are different to the Allocated Invoiced Amounts.-Cause-In the same proportional manner, as a Sales Document Item's Allocated amount is calculated based on the Standalone Selling Price (SSP), also the Allocated Invoiced Amount of the POB IDs is calculated on a proportional basis.-Resolution-The formula to calculate a POB ID's Allocated Invoiced amount is:-(SSP of POB ÷ Total SSP of all Sales order Items/POB IDs of the RAC)  x Total Invoiced Revenue amount.-Example:-Total SSP: 3000,00 LC-Total Invoiced Revenue: 3200,00 LC-Sales Order Item POB ID POB SSP Invoiced Revenue Formula Allocated Invoiced Amount-ABC-AA XYZ-AA   600,00 LC 750,00 LC   (600/3000) x 3200=  640,00 LC-ABC-BB XYZ-BB 1200,00 LC 1100,00 LC (1200/3000) x 3200 = 1280,00 LC-ABC-CC XYZ-CC   700,00 LC 600,00 LC   (700/3000) x 3200 = 746,67 LC-ABC-DD XYZ-DD   500,00 LC 750,00 LC   (500/3000) x 3200 = 533,33 LC-Total:    3000,00 LC 3200,00 LC   3200,00 LC-See Also- IFRS 15 / ASC 606: Revenue Recognition Accounting-Keywords-Allocated Invoiced Amount, Invoiced Revenue, POB, RAC

Title: Unit Not Shown for Time Account Balance
Content: Symptom-You have noticed that some time accounts are missing their time units, which can be "day(s)" or "hour(s)", next to where their balances are shown.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Home work center-Access the Self-Services Overview-Click the View Time Accounts Overview link-Here, some accounts are missing the units next to their balance- Alternatively:-Go to the Time Administration work center-Access the Employees work center view-Search for any employee that has one of the affected time accounts assigned-Select it and click Edit-Navigate to the Time Account Balances tab-The unit of the time account balance is missing here as well-Cause-The unit might be blocked in the relevant fine-tuning activity of the Business Configuration work center.-Resolution-Go to the Business Configuration work center-Access the Overview work center view-Locate and open the Quantities and Units of Measure fine-tuning activity-Click the link to Create and Maintain Physical Units-Under Activation Status: 3 - Blocked, filter the Unit column for the ID of the unit that is not being shown. For reference, the IDs are:-"DAY" - Day(s)-"HUR" - Hour(s)-Change Activation Status to 2 - Released-Click Save or Save and Close-Keywords-Time Account, Balance, Unit, Missing, Day(s), Hour(s)

Title: Exchange Rate Postings after Bank Statement Processing for Assigned Payments
Content: Symptom-An invoice in foreign currency has been cleared against a self-initiated payment and exchange rate differences have been recognized. Subsequently a bank statement confirming this payment is processed and exchange rate differences are realized again. You are unsure about the nature and the calculation of the posted exchange rate differences.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-The exchange rate posting is caused by the posting of the payment allocation resulting from the bank statement upload. The allocation type is Payment Assignment. You can access relevant payment allocation either in:-Payment Management work center.-Navigate to the Payment Allocations view.-Select the relevant Payment Allocation.- -- or via the posted bank statement.-Go to the Liquidity Management work center.-Open the Bank Statements view.-Navigate to the relevant bank statement and Edit.-Follow the link Postprocessing required to access the relevant payment allocation.-You can access the resulting journal entry in the field Journal Entry ID. Here either an exchange rate loss or exchange rate gain is recognized against the G/L bank account.-Cause-The posting can be explained by the interplay of applied, differing exchange rates, bank account in foreign currency, invoice in foreign currency and clearing of foreign currency transactions in company currency.-Paying such an invoice with an applied differing exchange rate leads to the recognition of either an exchange rate loss or exchange rate gain. When subsequently this transaction is confirmed in a bank statement, further exchange rate loss/gain is realized in case the exchange rate has altered. The exchange rate difference previously posted is taken into consideration.-The exchange rate applied at a certain time can be derived from the Exchange Rate History found in the General Ledger work center under Common Tasks / Edit Exchange Rates.-Example:-The company currency is Canadian Dollar (CAD). After a bank statement upload 100 CAD are posted as exchange rate loss.-Supplier invoice XYZ over 1.000 USD is posted effective 01.06.2013. The exchange rate CAD/USD is 1,0. -On 01.07.2013 invoice XYZ is cleared with an outgoing check payment over 1.000 USD The exchange rate CAD/USD is 1,2. Consequently an exchange rate loss of 200 CAD is realized in clearing ABC. -The bank statement containing the 1.000 USD check payment is confirmed with a statement date 15.07.2013. The exchange rate CAD/USD is 1,3. This corresponds with a payment of 1.300 CAD in company currency for a supplier invoice over 1.000 CAD in company currency.-Since 200 CAD exchange rate loss have already been realized in clearing ABC, the remaining 100 CAD are recognized in in the payment allocation of type Payment Assignment against the G/L bank account representing the USD bank account.-

Title: Incoming Tax Return With Multiple Tax Payments
Content: Symptom-You have created a VAT Return with a tax receivable amount.-From your bank you receive two separate incoming payments via bank statement for this single tax return.-It is, however, not possible to assign more than one tax payment to a tax return.-How to clear both payments with the tax return?-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-In the Tax Management work center, navigate to the VAT Returns view.-Find the Reported tax return X with a tax receivable amount of, say, 100,00 LC (Local Currency).-In the Liquidity Management work center, in the Bank Statements view open the respective bank statement containing the two incoming payments of, say, 80,00 LC and 20,00 LC from the Tax Authority.-In the bank statement go to the Transactions tab.-For both payments (Payment Method: Other Incoming Payment) from the Tax Authority Post Processing is Required as the payments could not be allocated automatically.-Press on the Required links to open the Payment Allocations.-How to allocate the payments in order to clear the tax receivable amount of tax return X?-Cause-At the moment it is not supported to assign more than one payment to a tax return.-Resolution-But there is a workaround:-Use one payment allocation to create a tax payment and assign it to the incoming tax return.-Accept the payment difference (the difference amount equals the amount of the second payment).-Allocate the difference to a specific account with the second payment allocation.-1. Create the Tax Payment:-In the bank statements Transactions tab, click the Required link to access the first payment allocation over the amount of 80,00 LC.-In the Customer/Supplier ID field, select the Tax Authority.-In the Payment Allocated To field, select 8 - Tax payables or receivables.-In the Allocated Amount field, enter the amount of 80,00 LC. -Then click Post. This will automatically trigger the creation of the incoming tax payment.-2. Assign the Tax Return:-In the Tax Management work center, naviage to the Tax Payments view.-Here, in the Tax Payments in Preparation screen, select the new tax payment A over 80,00 LC and press View.-In the Tax Return Arrangement ID select the ID valid during the dates of tax return X. -In the Tax Payments tab match tax return X to the tax payment.-A Payment Difference Amount of 20,00 LC is displayed.-Press Accept.-After the tax payment has been released the tax return X is cleared and its status now changes to Completed.-3. Allocate the Payment Difference:-In the Tax Payments view of the Tax Management work center, open the now released tax payment A.-Click the Journal Entry ID of the payment to check which G/L account the payment difference has been allocated to. Note down the G/L account XYZ.-Now go back to the bank statement's Transactions tab in the Liquidity Management work center and click the Required link to access the second payment allocation B over 20,00 LC.-In the Payment Allocation, navigate to the Allocation to G/L Account tab.-In the G/L Account column, select the Account Determination group to which G/L account XYZ is assigned.*-In the Credit Gross Amount column, enter the payment/ tax payment difference amount of 20,00 LC.-Click Post.-This way tax return X is cleared with tax payment A.-And the payment difference is cleared via the direct G/L Account posting in Payment Allocation B.-*Should G/L Account XYZ not be available for payment allocations select an appropriate account determination group of your choice. In a last step create a Journal Entry Voucher to post the amount to G/L account XYZ.-Keywords-tax payment, vat return; multiple tax payments

Title: Workflow Rules For Suppliers not Working as Expected
Content: Symptom-You maintained two Workflow Rules for Suppliers, one for Bank Data and the other one for Purchasing Data. You noticed that when changing the payment data, a notification from both workflow rules are being sent.-However, only one workflow should be triggered.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign 2205 and higher.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Application and User Management work center.-Then go to the Workflow Rules view.-Create the two Workflow Rules for Suppliers, one for Bank Data and the other one for Purchasing Data.-Once it's finished, change the payment data of a supplier.-You will receive a notification from both Workflow Rules.-Cause-Currently, this is the expected system behavior.-Resolution-Although this is the expected system behavior, we would suggest you to do the following:-We would recommend to slightly change the modeling of your two workflow rules for detection of changed bank data and purchasing data, respectively.-For the purpose of such a detection we have delivered simple Boolean fields: "Bank Data Changed" which delivers a "true" in case any relevant part of the bank data has changed, "Purchasing Data Changed" which delivers a "true" in case any relevant part of the purchasing data has been changed.-You can enter the necessary condition in the following way:-Example:-Workflow rule for "Bank Data Changed": As Field: "Bank Data Changed" (do not check the "Value Before Object Change") Compare Operator: "Equal to" With: "Value" and check the checkbox right to the "Value"-This should be enough, as you only need this one Group.--Then the same with the workflow rule for "Purchasing Data Changed"  - here, of course, you might want to select the field "Purchasing Data Changed".-After that, the conditions for the workflow trigger should no longer overlap and the notification should only be triggered once in case you only change one of the data sets.-Keywords-Workflow Rules, Workflow Rules for Suppliers, Bank Data, Purchasing Data, Notification, Sending twice, duplicated,

Title: Error Message "Bank Data Not Found; Check if Bank Data Was Migrated with Employee Data" During Migration of Personnel Administration Data
Content: Symptom-You are trying to migrate Personnel Administration data in the migration tool, but the migration fails with error message "Bank data not found; check if bank data was migrated with employee data."-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Business Configuration Work center-Access the Overview work center view-Search for "migration of employee data"-Open the relevant country/region-specific fine-tuning activity-Click the link to Migrate personnel administration data using the migration tool-In the migration tool, select the relevant migration file-Click the Execute Migration button, then select Execute Migration Step by Step-Error occurs on step 3 - Simulate Import-Cause-The Bank Details which are being migrated in the Personnel Administration migration are not the same that were migrated in the basic Employee Data migration.-Resolution-According to the functionality of system, the account details which were migrated with the basic Employee Data migration and the account details being migrated with the Personnel Administration data migration should be same. Please correct the data in the Personnel Administration data to solve the issue.-Also the data is case sensitive i.e., the data should be in either upper or lower case depending upon the data migrated with basic Employee Data migration. For example, if the National Bank Code is MX in Basic employee data then it should same in Personnel Administration. If you enter Mx then the above will be raised--If you want to add a bank account different from the one migrated with the basic Employee Data migration, this should be done through the UI in the Personnel Administration work center after the migration has been completed.-See Also- 2742251 - Error "Bank ID XXXX Not Assigned to Employee" When Migrating the Personnel Administration Data-Keywords-Migrate Employee, Bank details, HR master data

Title: Is it Possible to Create a New Purchase Category?
Content: Symptom-A new Purchase Category needs to be created.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Go to the Overview view.-Search and open the activity Charts of Accounts, Financial Reporting Structures, Account Determination.-Under Account Determination, select Accounts Payable.-Select the In Transit tab.-The table displays the Purchase Categories S - Service Purchases, F - Fixed Asset Purchases, and M - Material Purchases. A new Purchase Category is expected to be created.-Cause-It is not possible to create new Purchase Categories. SAP Business ByDesign supports a standard set of Purchase Categories that cannot be extended.-Resolution-The G/L Account Substitution PDI feature can be used to determine whether it meets the requirement.-Keywords-Purchase Category, new, Account Determination, PDI, Business Configuration

Title: Error Message "Sales Organization XYZ Cannot Be Below Sales Organization ABC"
Content: Symptom-While checking the consistency of an org structure during activation, system throws the below error message:-"DD.MM.YYYY to DD1.MM1.YYYY1; sales organization XYZ cannot be below sales organization ABC" (where XYZ stands for the first org unit's ID and ABC stands for the second org unit's ID, parent of the first)-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Organizational Management work center.-Select Edit Org Structures under Common tasks.-Select one of the relevant org units, ABC or XYZ.-Click the Check button and choose Check Selected Structure.-Cause-The cause for the error message is due to the fact that on the dates mentioned in the error message, org unit XYZ was maintained as sales organization. At the same time, org unit ABC is also a sales organization.-The sales organization represents the top org unit of a sales hierarchy—as such, there should be only one in each hierarchy.-Resolution-Go to the Organizational Management work center.-Select Edit Org Structures under Common tasks.-Change the Effective Date to the first mentioned date in the error message.-Select the Org unit XYZ.-Go to Functions tab.-Uncheck the Sales Organization box.-Click the Save button.-After this, it should be possible to check and activate the org structure successfully.-Keywords-Sales Organization, Below, Org Structure

Title: Not All Tax Codes Are Available When Creating a Down Payment Request
Content: Symptom-You create a new Down Payment request and maintained your own Tax Codes in the Business Configuration Activiy 'Tax on Goods and Services'-However, these are not available in the dropdown list.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Open the Business Configuration work centre.-Find and Open the Tax on Goods and Services Activity.-Open Define Tax Codes.- You can see here all Tax Codes starting with a Alphabet .-Go to the Supplier Invoicing work centre.-Go to the Common Tasks sub view.-Click New Down payment Request.-Fill in Buying Company XYZ and select a ABC (XYZ represents the Company ID; ABC represents the Product ID).- The Tax Codes which are maintained in Business Configuration starting with a Alphabet are not available in the dropdown list.-Cause-The tax codes which are not 100% deductible are not shown in down payment request.-Resolution-When a company creates a Down Payment for a Supplier, the Tax Amounts should be fully deductible. That means that once the taxes are reported in the supplier invoices, the company can claim the credit against the taxes reported in the down payment. If the Tax Code in the Down Payment is non-deductible, those taxes will be considered as expense for the Company and then they can never claim that money back.-Keywords-Anzahlungsanforderung, Steuerkennzeichen,-missing,down payment request,tax codes

Title: Error message Check Storage Inconsistent when trying to Close or Block a Check Storage
Content: Symptom-You want to block or close a Check Storage but the Save action fails and the error message 'Check storage inconsistent' appears.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Liquidity Management work center.-Go to the Master Data view.-Select the Check Storage sub-view.-Search and open the check storage ID XXX (XXX represents the check storage ID).-Select the field Blocked.-Maintain the fields 'Valid From' and 'Valid To' as required.-Press 'Save' or 'Save and Close'.-The Save Action fails and the error message 'Check storage inconsistent' appears.-Cause-One reason for this error can be that the status of the Deposit Bank Account used in the creation of the Check Storage is obsolete.-You can confirm this by double-clicking the Deposit Bank Account ID in the Check Storage.-Another reason could be that the validity status of the Company used in the creation of the Check Storage is not active.-You can check this by double-clicking the Company ID to confirm if its validity is already expired.-Resolution-There is a logic in place and it is only satisfied if the associated bank account is 'Active' and the respective company is valid on the selected dates.-Keywords-Check Storage, Block, Close.

Title: The Arrow Up For Item Level Discount List is Grayed Out
Content: Symptom-When you go to the Price Strategy the arrow up for item level discount list is grayed out.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Select your Project and click on the Open Activity List.-In the Fine-Tune step, open the fine-tuning activity Configure Price Strategy.-Click on the Access Sequences hyperlink.-Select custom pricing table CUSABC (CUSABC represents the ID of the pricing table).-Cause-For a Price List or a Discount List, the sorting is not relevant on item level, therefore it is grayed out.-Resolution-This is expected system behavior.-Keywords-Discount List;

Title: Custom Party Role is not Copied when creating an Invoice
Content: Symptom-A Custom Party Role is not Copied when creating an Invoice.-Environment- SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue--1. Go to the Sales Order Work Center.-2. Select the Sales Order View.-3. Search for the Sales Order ABC (Where ABC represents the number of the sales order).-4. Click on Edit and View All.-5. Navigate to Involved Parties.-The Custom Parties are available here.-1. Go to Customer Invoicing Work Center.-2. Select the Invoice Document View.-3. Search for the Invoice Document DEF (Where DEF represents the number of the Invoice).-4. Click on Edit and View All.-5. Navigate to Involved Parties.-The Custom Parties are not here.-Cause-This Custom Party is not on the Sales Orders Involved Parties, so this will not be copied to the Invoice Document.-Resolution-The system does not support adding custom parties to Customer Inovoices. This is the expected system behavior.-Keywords-Involved Parties; Invoice; Parties Role

Title: Error Message "User Account Not in Validity Date" When Logging Into System
Content: Symptom-When a user tries to log into their system with their user ID and password, system raises error message "User account not in validity date."-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-SAP Cloud for Customer-Reproducing the Issue-Access the tenant's URL in a web browser.-In the logon screen, enter user ID and password.-Click the Log On (SAP Business ByDesign) or Sign In (SAP Cloud for Customer) button.-Error message is raised.-Cause-The business user's Valid To date was set to a date in the past, meaning that the user is not valid in the current date.-Resolution-To resolve this issue, a system administrator needs to extend the validity of the affected user so that the new validity includes the current.-To do that, please follow the below steps:-Go to Business Users work center view.-In SAP Business ByDesign, within the Application and User Management work center-In SAP Cloud for Customer, within the Administrator work center.-Change the selection to All Business Users.-Using the search bar, locate the relevant business user.-Click the Edit button, then select Attributes.-In the Valid To field, set the date to a date in the future.-Click the Save (or Save and Close) button.-Once the user's validity is extended, they will once again be able to log onto the system using their credentials.-Keywords-User Account Not in Validity Date, Logon, Business User, Credentials-logon,logon failed,login

Title: Org Unit is not Available in the Access Restriction tab of a Business Role
Content: Symptom-You are trying to configure the Access Restrictions of a particular Business Role and when trying to find a specific Org Unit for the Work Center View Name BPM_ACCOUNTS, the Org Unit is not available.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign 2205 and higher.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Application and User Management Work Center.-Business Roles view.-Search for the required Business Role and select it.-Click Edit.-Go to the Access Restrictions tab.-Select Work Center View Name BPM_ACCOUNTS.-In the Restriction Rule section, click Find and search for the required Org Unit/Employee.-Cause-The required Org Unit is not assigned as Sales Organizational and Sales in the Functions tab.-Resolution-In order to have the Org Unit in the access restriction, you must to make the required Org Unit as a Sales Organizational and Sales in the Functions tab.-Go to the Organizational Management Work Center.-Go to the Org Structures view.-Click Edit.-Search for the Required Org Unit ID.-Select it and go to the Functions tab.-Check the options of Sales Organizational and Sales.-By doing that, the Org Unit will appear in the Access Restriction tab.-Keywords-Org Unit, Employee, Not Available, Missing, Business Role, BPM_ACCOUNTS.

Title: Dump Occurs When Revaluate Lease Contract
Content: Symptom-Dump occurs when you revaluate a lease contract.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Lease Contract Management work center.-Go to Lease Contract view.-Select contract XYZ. (XYZ stands for the lease contract ID)-Select Actions -> Revaluate.-System crashes.-Cause-The latest version of the lease contract has the same start date and end date, so when system triggers a recalculation (with the revaluate action), it ends up trying to divide by zero (term length when start and end dates are the same), which causes the error. Because the lease is still in revision, the original dates show up in the UI, but you can check the latest dates in the versions tab from which the system takes the dates for the revaluation.-Resolution-You need to create a new version where start and end dates are not the same, and this should solve the issue.-Keywords-Lease Contract, Revaluate

Title: Journal - Italy: PDF File Is Missing
Content: Symptom-You are trying to get the PDF file of the statutory report Journal - Italy for the period DD.MM.YYYY-DD.MM.YYYY, but the button View Printed Results is grayed out.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to General Ledger work center. -Go to Statutory Reports subview.-Click Journal - Italy.-You will see the PDF file of the statutory report Journal - Italy for the period DD.MM.YYYY-DD.MM.YYYY has not been created. The button View Printed Results is grayed out.-Cause-This issue is due to incorrect usage of report.-In the scenarios where data exceeds the permissible limit while processing it (on click of the Next button), we recommend using the schedule option so that processing of a large amount of data can be handled.-There are two options for schedule:-Schedule -> This option generates the data.-Schedule and Print -> This option generates the data and creates the PDF file.-Whatever option is chosen, the report status will change to Finished.-The status Released will be set when the Release button is clicked, this freezes the report parameters and results.-Resolution-You need to use the Schedule and Print option to generate the PDF for running with a large amount of data.-See Also-Quick Guide for Journal Reporting – Italy-Keywords-button View Printed Results is grayed out; Missing Journal - Italy PDF file; Journal - Italy; Finished; Release; statutory report

Title: Wrong Product Category Displayed in the List Price
Content: Symptom-You changed the Product Category of a product however the List Price is still showing the old value.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Product Portfolio work center.-Go to List Prices view. -In the Advanced Filter, filter for the product ID. -In the results you can see that the current active List Price for this product shows the wrong Product Category ID.-Cause-The Product Category will only be updated in currently active List Prices. It means that the List Price was not currently 'Active' when the change was made in the product's master data.-Resolution-First you need to maintain the List Price as active:-Go to Product Portfolio work center.-Go to List Prices view. -Search for the List Price ID. -Click in Release button and select Release. -Then you can perform a dummy change in the Product's master data so the List Price is updated. For example, you can change the Product Category and then change it back.-Keywords-List Price, Product Category, Master Data

Title: Error During Fixed Asset Manual Posting - Revaluation : Offsetting Item Data Are Not Required
Content: Symptom-You are trying to post Manual Posting - Revaluation for a fixed asset and encountered the error message "Offsetting Item Data Are Not Required".- Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Fixed Assets work center.-Select the Fixed Asset XYZ.-You can either Edit the asset and then apply manual postings or directly access this feature by choosing Manual Posting.-Choose Revaluation.-Fill in all required parameters like Set of Books, dates, Valuation View, Revaluation Of, account etc.,-Either Post or Simulate the resulting journal entry.-The error "Offsetting Item Data Are Not Required" appears.-Cause-You have selected the valuation view XX - which is statistical in nature and for this no postings will get generated so the assignment of Offsetting GL account is also not required.-Resolution-For statistical valuation views there is no need to enter a general ledger account under Offsetting Account Assignment. An offsetting account assignment is only required for book depreciation valuation views.-Example:-For 1 - Book depreciation it is required to enter a GL Account under offsetting account assignment field.-For 10 - Federal tax ACRS/MACRS - with bonus it is not required to enter a GL Account under offsetting account assignment field.-Keywords-offsetting item date are not required

Title: How to Correctly Record the Outgoing Payments Made Outside of SAP Business ByDesign into the System
Content: Symptom-You make an outgoing bank transfer payment outside of SAP Business ByDesign system, now you want to record it into the system through the following ways:-Create a journal entry voucher to reflect the payment in the system, and deduct the amount from the related bank account. But this journal entry voucher does not appear as the item to be selected when creating a bank statement.-Create an outgoing bank transfer from the Payment Management work center to record this outgoing payment, but the outgoing bank transfer requires a payee and a payee bank, which does not apply to your scenario, because the manual outgoing payment you made does not involve a specific payee.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-First of all, follow the steps below to record the outgoing payment by creating a journal entry voucher:-Go to the General Ledger work center, and select the Journal Entries view.-Select the Journal Entry Vouchers subview.-Choose New and then select Journal Entry Voucher.-Enter the necessary information.-In the line items, enter a credit amount to the G/L account related to the bank account XYZ (XYZ means the Bank Account ID), and the same debit amount to a G/L account, for example, an expense account.-Post it.-Then go to the Liquidity Management work center, and select the New Bank Statement under Common Tasks.-In the Bank Account ID field, enter bank account XYZ, and then fill the other mandatory fields.-Navigate to the second step Select Items, you cannot see the journal entry voucher created earlier from the items list.  -Then follow the steps below to create an outgoing bank transfer:-Go to the Payment Management work center, and choose New Outgoing Bank Transfer under Common Tasks.-You could see that Payee and Payee Bank are mandatory fields, which are not applicable in your case.-Cause-A journal entry voucher is a transaction that you enter directly in accounting to generate journal entries. It can make adjusting/correcting entries to the G/L accounts, make manual postings on fixed assets, correct or adjust automatic postings etc. But it cannot directly make changes to a bank account. A bank account is different from a G/L account, even if with the same name. So creating a journal entry voucher is by no means the correct way to record the outgoing payments into the system.-Resolution-To record the outgoing payment in the system without setting the Payee and Payee Bank, and deduct the amount for the bank account XYZ, follow the steps below:-First of all, reverse the journal entry voucher posted earlier.-Then go to the Liquidity management work center, create a new bank statement.-In the Enter General Data step, enter the necessary information such as Company and Opening Balance etc.-In the Bank Account ID field, enter XYZ.-Choose Next, and go to the third step Create and Edit Items.-Choose Add Row.-In the Payment Method field, select the appropriate outgoing payment method, for example, Outgoing Bank Transfer or Other Outgoing Payments.-Enter the Debit Amount.-Meanwhile, the Further Processing field is automatically set as Required, which means a Payment Allocation task is created for you to take manual action.-Release the bank statement.-View the bank statement created above, and then go to the Transactions tab.-Select the item you add for the manual outgoing payment, and click Required.-The system opens up the payment allocation.-Go to the Other Allocation tab, and choose Add Row to directly allocate this payment to a G/L account.-Release the payment allocation.-   The payment is now correctly recorded in the system.-Keywords-outgoing payment; payee

Title: The Field "Send By" Does Not Get Filled In Automatically when Creating New Purchase Order
Content: Symptom-When creating a new Purchase Order, you are adding a Supplier ABC (ABC being the Supplier ID), but the field "Send By" remains empty despite the Output Channel being correctly maintained in Supplier Master Data (e-mail, XML, Printer...).-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to work center Purchase Requests and Orders.-Select New Purchase Order-From the basic view, add the Supplier ABC-The field "Send By" stays empty.-Cause-The question "Do you want to send the process-integrated output documents via multiple output channels?" is currently selected in your Implementation Project.-Resolution-Go to work center Business Configuration.-Click "Edit Project Scope".-Click Next until the Questions tab.-Select the Scoping Element Communication and Information Exchange > Business Process Management > Process-Integrated Input and Output Management.-Find the question "Do you want to send the process-integrated output documents via multiple output channels?", unselect it and save.-Keywords-New Purchase Orders; Send By; Output Management; Multiple Output Channels;

Title: Error "Update not possible; specified data for SERVPROD_VALU_DATA-COST_RATE with key SET_OF_BOOKS_ID-CONTENT AND VALIDITY_DA does not exist" While Migrating the Service Valuation Data
Content: Symptom-Your requirement is to migrate Service Valuation Data using the migration tool.-During the simulation you receive the below error:-"Error detected in source record with key value 'ABC, DEF'-Update not possible; specified data for SERVPROD_VALU_DATA-COST_RATE with key SET_OF_BOOKS_ID-CONTENT = `GHI` AND VALIDITY_DA does not exist"-ABC means the Service ID.-DEF means the Company ID.-GHI means the Set of Books ID.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Business Configuration work center.-Select the Implementation Projects view or Overview view.-Search and Open the activity Migration of Service Valuation Data.-Choose Migrate service valuation data using the migration tool.-Execute Migration for the respective Migration File with migration mode Add new records.-In the Simulation step, you receive the mentioned error.-Cause-At least one of the services for which you are migrating valuation data do not exist in the system. You may verify this in the Services view in Product Data work center.-The error message does not necessarily mean that respective Service ID ABC does not exist in the system.-When migrating the file the system use packaging, meaning that it concurrently simulate/import a bunch of records instead of doing each one at a time. This is great for improving performance, however, as a side effect it might happen that when one record in a package fails, the entire package fails with the same error even though it's not an issue for those records.-Resolution-If any of the Service IDs are not available in the system, you will not be able to migrate the Service Valuation Data. Before you try to upload the Service Valuation Data, ensure that all Service IDs present in the Migration of Service Valuation Data file exist in system. To upload the Services, you may use the activity Migration of Services.-Keywords-Service Valuation Data, SERVPROD_VALU_DATA-COST_RATE, SET_OF_BOOKS_ID-CONTENT, Services Migration, Services

Title: Expense Reports Containing Only Paid By Company Expenses Will not be Reimbursed to Employee
Content: Symptom-You have submitted an Expense Report XYZ and it has passed Approval and Audit process but the Expenses amounts are not reimbursed to Employee.-XYZ means the expense report ID.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign-Reproducing the Issue-Go to the Travel and Expenses Work center.-Go to the Expense Reports view.-Show All Expense Reports and Find Expense Report XYZ.-Choose Expense Report XYZ hyperlink.-Go to the Document Flow tab.-You also notice that the Reimbursement Status is No Reimbursement Requested under Expense and Reimbursement Summary in the Overview screen.-Cause-Expense Report contains only Paid by Company Expenses and hence Expenses will not be paid out to Employee.-This can be checked by the following steps:-Go to the Business Configuration Work center.-Go to the Implementation Projects view.-Select the Implementation Project and Choose Open Activity List.-Go to the Fine-Tune Chevron.-Show All Activities and Find Activity Expense Reporting - Country version of Employee.-Go to Edit Expense Types.-Sort the Expense Types using Filter.-When you select the Expense Type, you could see under the Definition tab the field Payment/Taxation shows Paid by Company.-Resolution-System works as designed.-Keywords-Travel and Expense. Expense Report. Paid By Company

Title: Goods and Service Receipt Merged in Supplier Invoice
Content: Symptom-Supplier Invoice merge two Goods and Service Receipt in one line with one location and one Tax Region/Code.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to Purchase Requests and Orders work center.-Go to Purchase Orders view.-Filter for All Purchase Orders.-Search for ABC and open it (ABC represents the Purchase Order ID).-Click in view all and go to Document Flow tab.-See two Goods and Service Receipts.-Open one of the Receipts, click in view all.-In the Items tab and Delivery subtab see that the Delivery Address is different between the two Receipts.-Go to Supplier Invoice work center.-Go to Invoice Entry view.-Search for ABC.-Click in New Invoice.-See that the system is merging Supplier Invoice with the two Goods and Services Receipt with one line of items, one location and one Tax Region/Code.-Cause-System behavior.-Resolution-The system is merging the lines from the Goods and Service Receipt because they are from the same line in the Purchase Orders and in the Purchase Order the ship-to is from one place only, so system understand it as two different deliveries at the same place, and that is why even if you do an Invoice directly from Goods and Service Receipt, selecting two Goods and Service Receipt, the system will merge in one line.-If you want that the system does not merge, you can add 2 lines in the Purchase Order with different ship-to, in that way you can make two different Goods and Service Receipt and just one invoice, and it will display as two different lines in the invoice.-Keywords-Supplier Invoice; Goods and Service Receipt; Purchase Order;

Title: Error ‘Business Transaction Expense Report XYZ : Tax Country not supported’
Content: Symptom-You are trying to post an Expense Report from Concur, but you are getting an error message saying that the Tax country is not supported.-Environment-SAP Business ByDesign.-Reproducing the Issue-Go to General Ledger work center.-Go to Expense Reports subview.-Select All Expense Reports and search for Report ID ABC (ABC represents the Report ID).-You will see the error message:-'Business Transaction Expense Report XYZ (XYZ represents the Report Key): Tax Country not supported'-Cause-Countries Brazil and Mexico are not supported by Financial notification (which is what any external transaction coming into SAP Business ByDesign will create). So, the Concur expense report is external and tries to create a financial notification but it cannot as it's not supported.-Resolution-In the SAP Business ByDesign and Concur Integration Guide itself, there is a list of supported countries. Some unlisted countries may work with SAP Business ByDesign but Brazil and Mexico will not.-Keywords-Expense report. Tax Country not supported. Business Transaction Expense Report. Tax. Concur.

Title: Missing Country in Preview of Purchase Order Form
